questions.q: The Sun appears to move from east to west across the sky. What does this imply about Earth’s rotation?
options: A) Earth rotates from east to west.
B) Earth rotates from west to east.
C) Earth rotates from north to south.
D) Earth does not rotate; only the Sun moves.
questions.answer: B) Earth rotates from west to east.
questions.explanation: The Exemplar directly connects the apparent daily motion of the Sun with Earth’s rotation. An apparent east-to-west motion of the sky results from Earth rotating in the opposite direction. Therefore Earth rotates from west to east.

questions.q: A newly discovered planet lies between Uranus and Neptune. Which statement about its orbital period is most consistent with the Exemplar?
options: A) It should be shorter than Uranus’s period.
B) It should be longer than Neptune’s period.
C) It should be greater than Uranus’s period but less than Neptune’s period.
D) It must equal Earth’s period.
questions.answer: C) It should be greater than Uranus’s period but less than Neptune’s period.
questions.explanation: The source asks about a hypothetical planet between Uranus and Neptune. Planets farther from the Sun have longer orbital periods, so a planet between those two should have an intermediate period. Thus its period should exceed Uranus’s but remain less than Neptune’s.

questions.q: A bright object in the night sky does not twinkle and changes its position with respect to the background stars over time. Which identification is best supported?
options: D) A meteor that remains permanently in one place
questions.explanation: The Exemplar contrasts stars and planets by noting that planets generally do not twinkle and change position relative to stars. A bright non-twinkling object with changing position therefore fits the behaviour of a planet. The observation does not match a fixed star such as the Pole Star.

questions.q: If the first day of a month is a new moon day, what should be expected around the fifteenth day?
options: A) Another new moon because the lunar cycle is 15 days long
B) A full moon, approximately half a lunar cycle after new moon
C) No Moon because the Moon stops reflecting sunlight
questions.answer: B) A full moon, approximately half a lunar cycle after new moon
questions.explanation: The Exemplar asks what phase should occur on the fifteenth when the first is a new moon. Roughly half a lunar cycle after new moon, the Earth-facing half of the Moon appears fully illuminated. Therefore the expected phase is a full moon.
